title.zh: 卷455 列傳二百四十二 董福祥 张俊 夏辛酉 金运昌 黄万鹏 余虎恩 桂锡桢 方友升
title.en: Volume 455 Biographies 242: Dong Fuxiang, Zhang Jun, Xia Xinyou, Jin Yunchang, Huang Wanpeng, Yu Huen, Gui Xizhen, Fang Yousheng
title.raw: 卷455 列傳二百四十二 董福祥 张俊 夏辛酉 金运昌 黄万鹏 余虎恩 桂锡桢 方友升

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四十二

translations.literal: Biographies 242
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 242

sentences.zh: 董福祥張俊夏辛酉金運昌黃萬鵬餘虎恩桂錫楨方友升

translations.literal: Dong Fuxiang, Zhang Jun, Xia Xinyou, Jin Yunchang, Huang Wanpeng, Yu Huen, Gui Xizhen, Fang Yousheng
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fuxiang, Zhang Jun, Xia Xinyou, Jin Yunchang, Huang Wanpeng, Yu Huen, Gui Xizhen, and Fang Yousheng

sentences.zh: 董福祥，字星五，甘肅固原人。

translations.literal: Dong Fuxiang, style name Xingwu, was a native of Guyuan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fuxiang, whose style name was Xingwu, came from Guyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 同治初，回亂作，鳳、邠、汧、瀧寇氛殆遍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, the Hui rebellion broke out, and the aura of banditry nearly spread throughout Feng, Bin, Qian, and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi era, when the Muslim uprising erupted, rebel activity had nearly engulfed Fengxiang, Binzhou, Longzhou, and the Longdong region.

sentences.zh: 福祥亦起安化，與其州人張俊、李雙良蹂躪陝、甘十數州縣，竊據花馬池，犯綏德，窺榆林，潰勇、饑民附之，眾常十餘萬。

translations.literal: Fuxiang also rose in Anhua, and with his fellow townsman Zhang Jun and Li Shuangliang ravaged more than a dozen prefectures and counties in Shaanxi and Gansu, secretly holding Huamachi, invading Suide, and coveting Yulin; routed braves and starving people attached themselves to him, and his forces often exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang likewise rose in Anhua. Together with his fellow townsman Zhang Jun and Li Shuangliang, he ravaged more than a dozen counties across Shaanxi and Gansu, seized Huamachi, struck at Suide, and menaced Yulin. Routed soldiers and starving civilians flocked to his banner, and his following often surpassed one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 嗣為劉松山所敗，其父世猷降，福祥亦率眾乞歸款。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated by Liu Songshan; his father Shiyou surrendered, and Fuxiang also led his masses to beg to return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He was later defeated by Liu Songshan. His father Shiyou surrendered, and Fuxiang too led his men in suing for pardon and submission.

sentences.zh: 乃簡其精銳者，編為董字三營：福祥居中營，俊居左，雙良居右。

translations.literal: Thereupon the elite were selected and organized into three battalions under the character Dong: Fuxiang held the center battalion, Jun the left, and Shuangliang the right.
translations.idiomatic: The best troops were then picked out and formed into three battalions bearing the character Dong: Fuxiang commanded the center, Jun the left wing, and Shuangliang the right.

sentences.zh: 從攻金積堡，福祥襲卡後，被創不少卻，破其禮拜寺。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jinjibao, Fuxiang raided behind the stockade, was wounded yet did not retreat much, and destroyed their mosque.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Jinjibao, Fuxiang struck from behind the stockade. Though wounded, he scarcely fell back and smashed their mosque.

sentences.zh: 頓板橋，寇來爭，與蕭章開夾擊敗之，金積堡平，超授都司。

translations.literal: He halted at Banqiao; the rebels came to contest it, and with Xiao Zhangkai he pincered and defeated them; Jinjibao was pacified, and he was specially promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Banqiao the rebels came to fight for the position; Fuxiang and Xiao Zhangkai caught them in a pincer and routed them. When Jinjibao fell, he was promoted out of turn to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從劉錦棠至碾伯，趨峽口，與陝回禹得彥、雀三大戰，破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed Liu Jintang to Nianbo, hastened to Xiakou, and fought a great battle with the Shaanxi Hui leaders Yu Deyan and Que San, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he marched with Liu Jintang to Nianbo and pressed on to Xiakou, where he fought and broke the Shaanxi Muslim chiefs Yu Deyan and Que San in a major engagement.

sentences.zh: 進擊白彥虎於高家堡，焚其壘而還。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Bai Yanhu at Gaojiabao, burned his fort, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Bai Yanhu at Gaojiabao, burned his fortifications, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已而偽知府高桂源構彥虎圍西寧，撲雙良營，福祥又大敗之，圍解，遷游擊。

translations.literal: Before long the false prefect Gao Guiyuan incited Yanhu to besiege Xining and struck at Shuangliang's camp; Fuxiang again routed them greatly, the siege was lifted, and he was transferred to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the rebel prefect Gao Guiyuan induced Yanhu to invest Xining and assaulted Shuangliang's camp. Fuxiang routed them again, lifted the siege, and was promoted to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 徙守向陽堡城，复討平河州叛回，積功至提督。

translations.literal: He was moved to guard Xiangyangbao city, again campaigned to pacify the rebel Hui of Hezhou, and by accumulated merit rose to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to hold Xiangyangbao, he helped suppress the Muslim rebels of Hezhou and, through accumulated merit, rose to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，從出關，戰天山，會大風晝晦，吏士弗敢進。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he followed in the campaign beyond the pass, fought at Tianshan, and when a great wind made the day dark, officials and soldiers did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he marched beyond the pass and fought at Tianshan. A fierce wind darkened the sky at midday, and none of the officers or men dared press forward.

sentences.zh: 福祥率眾先登，一鼓殲之，又破之木壘河、古牧地，進复烏魯木齊諸城及瑪納斯南城。

translations.literal: Fuxiang led the masses to ascend first, destroyed them in one drumbeat, again defeated them at Mulei River and Gumudi, and advanced to recover the cities of Urumqi and the southern city of Manas.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang led his men up first and annihilated the enemy in a single charge. He then defeated them at Mulei River and Gumudi and went on to recover Urumqi and the southern quarter of Manas.

sentences.zh: 是時彥虎猶據開都河西岸，覬入俄。

translations.literal: At this time Yanhu still held the west bank of the Kaidu River and looked to enter Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhu still held the west bank of the Kaidu River and was seeking refuge in Russia.

sentences.zh: 福祥自阿哈布拉緣塗置哨壘，至曲惠而營，士卒儲薪草，濬井泉，以俟錦棠軍至，破之，复喀喇沙爾。

translations.literal: Fuxiang from Ahabula along the route set up sentry forts, encamped at Quhui, had soldiers store firewood and grass and dig wells, awaited Jintang's army to arrive, defeated them, and recovered Karashahr.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang marched from Ahabula, posting sentry forts along the route until he encamped at Quhui. His men stockpiled fuel and fodder and dug wells while waiting for Jintang's main force. When it arrived they broke the enemy and recovered Karashahr.

sentences.zh: 是冬，克和闐，南疆西四城告寧。

translations.literal: That winter he captured Khotan, and the four western cities of the southern frontier reported tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he took Khotan, and the four western cities of the southern Tarim were declared at peace.

sentences.zh: 繇是董軍名震西域。

translations.literal: From this the Dong army's name shook the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Dong troops were famed throughout the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂、世職，賜號阿爾杭阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was rewarded with the yellow jacket, a hereditary office, and granted the title Erhangabatulu.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he received the yellow jacket and a hereditary rank, and was granted the honorific Erhangabatulu.

sentences.zh: 安夷既就撫，布魯特酋阿布都勒哈誘之，復入寇色勒庫爾，北走庫倫，福祥馳之，抵空谷根滿，步卒足重繭，乃遴健者乘騾隊，從騎旅及之木吉。

translations.literal: After the An Yi had submitted, the Kirghiz chief Abdurehman enticed them, and they again invaded to raid Sarikol, fleeing north toward Kulun; Fuxiang galloped after them, reached Konggugenman, the foot soldiers' feet were heavily callused, so he selected the strong to ride mule teams and with the cavalry caught up at Muji.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Yi had been pacified, the Kirghiz chief Abdurehman incited them to rebel again. They raided Sarikol and fled north toward Kulun. Fuxiang raced in pursuit to Konggugenman. His infantry's feet were thick with calluses, so he picked out the hardiest men for mule teams and, with the cavalry, overtook the enemy at Muji.

sentences.zh: 寇方解鞍秣馬，驚起，依山而陣，俊敗之，福祥縱兵搜捕，复斬三百餘騎。

translations.literal: The rebels had just unsaddled to feed their horses and were startled up; they formed battle lines along the mountain; Jun defeated them, and Fuxiang loosed troops to search and seize, again beheading more than three hundred riders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had just unsaddled to water their horses when they were startled into action and drew up along the hillside. Jun routed them, and Fuxiang sent his men in pursuit, cutting down more than three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 自此寇不敢犯邊。

translations.literal: From this the rebels did not dare violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: After that the raiders no longer dared trouble the frontier.

sentences.zh: 授阿克蘇總兵，駐防喀城。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Aksu and garrisoned Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regional commander of Aksu and stationed his troops at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 未幾，而所部索餉譁變，戕營官胡登花，或請擊之，福祥曰：「營勇與叛勇有約，如昏夜響應，將奈何？

translations.literal: Before long his subordinates mutinied clamoring for pay and killed camp officer Hu Denghua; some urged attacking them, but Fuxiang said: "The camp braves and the mutinous braves have an agreement—if at dark of night they respond in concert, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Before long his troops mutinied over back pay and killed the camp officer Hu Denghua. Some urged an immediate assault, but Fuxiang said, "The loyal soldiers and the mutineers have made common cause. If they answer one another in the night, what then?

sentences.zh: 不如閉城守，彼勢孤必自斃也。

translations.literal: Better to close the city and defend; isolated in force they will surely destroy themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Better to shut the gates and hold the city. Cut off and alone, they will destroy themselves.

sentences.zh: 」越三日，悉為兵民擒獻，乃分別誅宥之。

translations.literal: " After three days all were seized and presented by soldiers and civilians, and he then separately executed or pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later soldiers and townspeople seized them all and handed them over. He then meted out execution or mercy as each case warranted.

sentences.zh: 事定，領俊及夏辛酉移駐葉爾羌、和闐。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he led Jun and Xia Xinyou to shift garrison to Yarkand and Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, he took Jun and Xia Xinyou with him to garrison Yarkand and Khotan.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢喀什噶爾提督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given the ministerial brevet rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received the brevet rank of minister.

sentences.zh: 會德攘膠澳，命率甘軍入衛。

translations.literal: When Germany seized Jiaozhou and Qingdao, he was ordered to lead the Gansu army to enter the capital guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Germany seized Jiaozhou and Qingdao, he was ordered to bring the Gansu army to the capital for palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 明年，西寧、碾伯又告警，督師還抵狄道。

translations.literal: The next year Xining and Nianbo again raised alarms; he supervised the army back and reached Didao.
translations.idiomatic: The following year alarms sounded again from Xining and Nianbo, and he led his army back as far as Didao.

sentences.zh: 河州馬永林叛，渡洮戰卻之，連破高家集、三甲集，道始通。

translations.literal: Ma Yonglin of Hezhou rebelled; he crossed the Tao River to fight and repelled them, successively breaking Gaojiaji and Sanjiaji, and the road was finally open.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yonglin of Hezhou rose in revolt. Fuxiang crossed the Tao River, beat him back, and in succession took Gaojiaji and Sanjiaji, reopening the route.

sentences.zh: 事寧，調甘肅。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When the disturbance was over, he was transferred to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 福祥自請援西寧。

translations.literal: Fuxiang himself requested to relieve Xining.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang volunteered to relieve Xining.

sentences.zh: 又明年，克上下五莊，乘勝復大通、多巴。

translations.literal: The year after next he captured the upper and lower Five Villages, and riding victory recovered Datong and Doba.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took the upper and lower Five Villages and, pressing his advantage, recovered Datong and Doba.

sentences.zh: 朝命駐西寧專剿撫，以魏光燾二十七營屬之。

translations.literal: The court ordered him to garrison Xining specializing in suppression and pacification, and placed Wei Guangcan's twenty-seven battalions under him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered him to station at Xining with sole charge of suppression and pacification, placing Wei Guangcan's twenty-seven battalions under his command.

sentences.zh: 會巴燕戎格、劉四复奔關外，福祥亟遣騎踵之，拔卡爾岡，先後夷海城、冶諸麻、甘州南山寇堡​​，關內外及青海悉平，加太子少保。

translations.literal: When Bayan Rongge and Liu Si again fled beyond the pass, Fuxiang urgently sent cavalry to follow on their heels, took Ka'ergang, and successively leveled the rebel forts of Haicheng, Yezhuma, and the southern hills of Ganzhou; inside and outside the pass and Qinghai were all pacified, and he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan Rongge and Liu Si fled beyond the pass again, Fuxiang sent cavalry in hot pursuit, seized Ka'ergang, and in turn destroyed the rebel strongholds at Haicheng, Yezhuma, and the southern hills of Ganzhou. The regions within and beyond the pass and all of Qinghai were pacified, and he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，入覲，命領武衛後軍，召對，福祥曰：「臣無他能，唯能殺外人耳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he entered court audience, was ordered to command the Rear Wuwei Army, was summoned to audience, and Fuxiang said: "Your servant has no other ability—only the ability to kill foreigners."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he came to court, was placed in command of the Rear Wuwei Army, and at an imperial audience said, "Your servant has no other talent—only the knack of killing foreigners."

sentences.zh: 」榮祿頗信仗之。

translations.literal: " Ronglu quite trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: " Ronglu came to rely on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 拳亂起，日本書記杉山彬出永定門，福祥兵殺之。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, the Japanese secretary Sugiyama Akira went out Yongding Gate, and Fuxiang's troops killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, the Japanese secretary Sugiyama Akira left the city through Yongding Gate, and Fuxiang's soldiers killed him.

sentences.zh: 於是董軍圍東交民巷，攻月餘不下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Dong army besieged the Legation Quarter, attacking for more than a month without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The Dong troops then besieged the Legation Quarter and assaulted it for more than a month without success.

sentences.zh: 敵兵自廣渠門入，福祥走彰儀門，縱兵大掠而西。

translations.literal: Enemy troops entered from Guangqu Gate; Fuxiang fled to Zhangyi Gate, loosed troops to plunder greatly, and went west.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy forces entered through Guangqu Gate. Fuxiang withdrew toward Zhangyi Gate, let his men loot freely, and marched west.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西幸，充隨扈大臣。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went west on tour, he served as accompanying guard minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager and Emperor fled west, he served on the imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 和議成，外人堅欲誅福祥。

translations.literal: When the peace agreement was concluded, the foreigners firmly wished to execute Fuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, the foreign powers insisted on executing Fuxiang.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章曰：「彼綰西陲軍寄久，慮激回變，當緩圖之。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang said: "He has long held the western frontier military trust; fearing to incite Hui rebellion, we should proceed slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang said, "He has long held military authority on the western frontier. We must fear provoking a Muslim uprising and should proceed cautiously."

sentences.zh: 」乃褫職錮於家。

translations.literal: " He was then stripped of office and confined at home.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of his post and placed under house arrest.

sentences.zh: 榮祿在西安綜大政，福祥移書讓之，略謂：「辱隸麾旌，任公指使，命攻使館，祥猶以殺使臣為疑。

translations.literal: Ronglu at Xi'an oversaw great government; Fuxiang sent a letter reproaching him, roughly saying: "Disgraced to serve under your banner, entrusted to your direction—ordered to attack the legations, yet Xiang still doubted killing envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Ronglu was directing affairs from Xi'an when Fuxiang wrote to reproach him, saying in substance, "Though I was shamed to serve under your banner and obeyed your orders to attack the legations, I still hesitated at the thought of killing foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 公言'僇力攘外，禍福同之'。

translations.literal: You said, 'Exert strength to repel outsiders—fortune and misfortune are shared.'
translations.idiomatic: You told me, 'Throw all our strength into driving out the foreigners—we share fortune and ruin alike.'

sentences.zh: 祥本武夫，恃公在上，故敢效奔走。

translations.literal: Xiang is originally a military man; relying on you above, therefore dared to render running service.
translations.idiomatic: I am only a soldier. Because you stood above me, I dared rush to do your bidding.

sentences.zh: 今公執政而祥被罪，祥死不足卹，如軍士憤懣何！

translations.literal: Now you hold power while Xiang is punished; Xiang's death is not worth grieving, but what of the soldiers' indignant resentment!
translations.idiomatic: Now you hold power while I am punished. My own death is nothing—but what of the fury of my soldiers!

sentences.zh: 」榮祿得書，置不答。

translations.literal: " Ronglu received the letter and set it aside without reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Ronglu received the letter and ignored it.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 其子天純，輸銀四十萬濟帑复官。

translations.literal: His son Tianchun paid four hundred thousand taels of silver to replenish the treasury and restore the office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianchun paid four hundred thousand taels of silver into the treasury to have the family's rank restored.

sentences.zh: 俊，字傑三。

translations.literal: Jun, style name Jiesan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, whose style name was Jiesan.

sentences.zh: 金積堡之役，與福祥並授都司。

translations.literal: In the Jinjibao campaign he and Fuxiang were together granted battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinjibao campaign he and Fuxiang were both promoted to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 規西寧，餘虎恩困峽口，俊力戰解之。

translations.literal: In the campaign for Xining, Yu Huen was trapped at Xiakou; Jun fought fiercely and relieved it.
translations.idiomatic: During the drive on Xining, Yu Huen was trapped at Xiakou; Jun fought hard and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 連破小峽、潤家溝，從攻河州、肅州，以戰功歷遷至副將，賜號倭興巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He successively broke Xiaoxia and Runjiagou, followed in attacking Hezhou and Suzhou, and by battle merit was promoted in succession to deputy commander, granted the title Woixingbatulu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xiaoxia and Runjiagou in turn, joined the assaults on Hezhou and Suzhou, and through repeated victories rose to deputy commander, receiving the honorific Woixingbatulu.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，從征西陲，复烏魯木齊，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Early in Guangxu he followed the western frontier campaign, recovered Urumqi, and was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu era he marched on the western frontier, helped recover Urumqi, and was promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 錦棠令入關募軍，於是成定遠三營。

translations.literal: Jintang ordered him to enter the pass to recruit troops, and thus were formed the three Dingyuan battalions.
translations.idiomatic: Jintang ordered him back inside the pass to raise troops, forming the three Dingyuan battalions.

sentences.zh: 先後從克東西四城，晉提督。

translations.literal: He successively followed in capturing the four eastern and western cities and was advanced to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the successive capture of the four western cities and was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 安夷复叛，俊倡議主剿，眾論譁起，錦棠獨韙之。

translations.literal: The An Yi rebelled again; Jun advocated chiefly for suppression; public opinion clamored; Jintang alone approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Yi rebelled again, Jun urged all-out suppression. Opinion in camp was divided, but Jintang alone sided with him.

sentences.zh: 寇竄庫倫，俊追至木吉，分三路入，戰良久，手刃執紅旗悍卒，寇愕走。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Kulun; Jun pursued to Muji, divided into three routes to enter, fought long, personally blade-killed a fierce soldier holding a red flag, and the rebels fled in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled toward Kulun. Jun pursued to Muji, split his force into three columns, and fought for hours. He personally killed a fierce warrior bearing a red flag, and the enemy broke in dismay.

sentences.zh: 進至卡拉阿提，會日已入，止舍。

translations.literal: Advancing to Kara'ati, as the sun had already set, he halted to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Kara'ati, but night had fallen and he made camp.

sentences.zh: 天未曙，整軍復進，日午及之。

translations.literal: Before dawn he arrayed the army and advanced again; at midday he caught up.
translations.idiomatic: Before daybreak he reformed his men and marched again, overtaking the enemy at noon.

sentences.zh: 寇不能反拒，槍矛所至，屍相填藉。

translations.literal: The rebels could not turn to resist; where spears and guns reached, corpses piled atop one another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels could not turn to fight. Where guns and spears reached, the dead lay in heaps.

sentences.zh: 抵黑子拉提、達坂，止餘數十騎，逾山入俄境，不復追。

translations.literal: Reaching Heizilati and Daban, only several dozen riders remained; they crossed the mountains into Russian territory, and he did not pursue further.
translations.idiomatic: At Heizilati and Daban only a few dozen horsemen were left. They crossed the mountains into Russian territory, and he did not pursue further.

sentences.zh: 是役，四晝夜馳八百餘裡，凡擒愛伊德爾呼里二人，安夷所謂「大通哈」也，胖色提以下數十人，猶華言「營官」。

translations.literal: In this campaign, in four days and nights he galloped more than eight hundred li, altogether capturing two Aiyide'erhuli—the An Yi term for "Datongha"—and several dozen men below Pangseti, still called in Chinese "camp officers."
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign he rode eight hundred li in four days and nights, capturing two Aiyide'erhuli—the An Yi title for "great commander"—and several dozen subordinates including Pangseti, whom the Chinese called camp officers.

sentences.zh: 賜頭品服、黃馬褂，授西寧鎮總兵，調伊犁。

translations.literal: He was granted first-rank court dress and the yellow jacket, appointed regional commander of Xining garrison, and transferred to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: He received first-rank court dress and the yellow jacket, was made regional commander of the Xining garrison, and was transferred to Ili.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，代福祥為喀什噶爾提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he replaced Fuxiang as provincial military commander of Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he succeeded Fuxiang as provincial military commander of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 尋還甘肅。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，入都，充武衛全軍翼長，兼統中軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he entered the capital, served as wing commander of the entire Wuwei Army, and concurrently commanded the center army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he came to the capital as wing commander of the full Wuwei Army and also commanded its center division.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，諡壯勤，予建祠。

translations.literal: The year after he died; posthumous title Zhuangqin; granted a memorial shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was posthumously titled Zhuangqin; a memorial shrine was granted.

sentences.zh: 俊好舞刀，所部衣幟皆白色，時稱「雪張」雲。

translations.literal: Jun was fond of brandishing the blade; his subordinates' clothing and banners were all white, and at the time he was called "Snow Zhang," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was famed for his swordplay. His troops wore white uniforms and flew white banners, earning him the nickname "Snow Zhang."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，字庚堂，籍山東鄆城。

translations.literal: Xinyou, style name Gengtang, registered origin Yuncheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Xinyou, whose style name was Gengtang, was registered in Yuncheng, Shandong.

sentences.zh: 初從僧格林沁討捻。

translations.literal: At first he followed Sengge Rinchen to suppress the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Sengge Rinchen in the campaign against the Nian rebels.

sentences.zh: 宗棠西征，從討陝回，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: When Zongtang marched west, he followed in suppressing the Shaanxi Hui and by accumulated merit rose to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On Zuo Zongtang's western expedition he helped suppress the Shaanxi Muslims and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 攻金積，裹創力戰，稱驍果。

translations.literal: Attacking Jinji, he wrapped his wounds and fought fiercely, and was called a valiant fighter.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Jinji he fought on though wounded and was hailed as a fierce warrior.

sentences.zh: 規肅州，充前鋒，拔塔爾灣、黃草壩，關內大定。

translations.literal: In the campaign for Suzhou he served as vanguard, took Ta'erwan and Huangcaoba, and the interior was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the drive on Suzhou he led the vanguard, captured Ta'erwan and Huangcaoba, and helped bring the interior to order.

sentences.zh: 數遷至游擊。

translations.literal: He was promoted several times to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 師出關，下阜康，襲黃田，破古牧，無役不從。

translations.literal: When the army went beyond the pass, he took Fukang, raided Huangtian, broke Gumudi—there was no campaign from which he was absent.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched beyond the pass he took Fukang, raided Huangtian, and stormed Gumudi, taking part in every engagement.

sentences.zh: 進規南路，攻托克遜。

translations.literal: He advanced to campaign on the southern route and attacked Toksun.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the southern route and assaulted Toksun.

sentences.zh: 彥虎子小虎殊死守，師行不得志，獨辛酉率遊軍數戰，略有斬擒。

translations.literal: Yanhu's son Xiaohu defended with exceptional tenacity; the army's advance was frustrated; only Xinyou led mobile troops in several battles and had some beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhu's son Xiaohu held out with desperate tenacity and the main army made little headway. Xinyou alone led mobile detachments in several skirmishes and managed a few kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 達坂之役，與餘虎恩輕騎先涉，列城左山岡。

translations.literal: In the Daban campaign, with Yu Huen he led light cavalry to ford first and drew up on the hillock left of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Daban he and Yu Huen forded ahead with light cavalry and took position on the hill to the city's left.

sentences.zh: 比回覺，悉力轟拒，師少卻。

translations.literal: When the Hui became aware, they poured all strength into cannon fire to repel, and the army retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslims realized what had happened, they opened a furious cannonade and the army fell back slightly.

sentences.zh: 辛酉斬先退者數人，乃止，卒大破之。

translations.literal: Xinyou beheaded several who retreated first, and only then did they halt; in the end he routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyou executed several men who had fled first, halted the retreat, and in the end won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 遷副將，賜號振勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commander and granted the title Zhenyongbatulu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy commander and granted the honorific Zhenyongbatulu.

sentences.zh: 從錦棠复庫車，至拜城，履冰抵上銅廠。

translations.literal: Following Jintang he recovered Kuche, reached Baicheng, and treading ice reached the upper copper works.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Jintang in recovering Kuche, pushed on to Baicheng, and crossed the ice to reach the upper copper mines.

sentences.zh: 回出盪，辛酉躍馬徑前，生擒貂衣賊一人。

translations.literal: The Hui came out to raid; Xinyou leaped his horse straight forward and captured alive one sable-coated rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslims sallied out to raid, Xinyou spurred straight ahead and took alive a rebel clad in sable fur.

sentences.zh: 回驚走，遂下阿克蘇。

translations.literal: The Hui fled in alarm, and Aksu was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Muslims fled in panic, and Aksu fell.

sentences.zh: 是時，帕夏奔葉爾羌，彥虎奔烏什。

translations.literal: At this time the Pasha fled to Yarkand and Yanhu fled to Ush.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Pasha fled to Yarkand and Yanhu to Ush.

sentences.zh: 錦棠專力討彥虎，令俊進擊，辛酉自西會之。

translations.literal: Jintang concentrated force on suppressing Yanhu, ordered Jun to advance and attack, and Xinyou joined from the west.
translations.idiomatic: Jintang focused on hunting Yanhu, ordered Jun to press the attack, and Xinyou joined from the west.

sentences.zh: 濟胡馬納克河，行戈壁八十里，破寇什城東，城拔，擢總兵，易勇號霍伽春。

translations.literal: Crossing the Khumalak River, marching eighty li through the Gobi, he broke the rebels east of Kashgar; the city was taken, he was promoted to regional commander, and his brave title was changed to Huoqiaochun.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Khumalak River, marched eighty li across the Gobi, and routed the enemy east of Kashgar. When the city fell he was promoted to regional commander and his honorific was changed to Huoqiaochun.

sentences.zh: 南疆平，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The southern frontier was pacified, and he was rewarded with the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern Tarim was pacified, he received the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 逸寇犯三台，辛酉隱勁騎衝殼罕山，誘之出。

translations.literal: Fugitive rebels invaded Santai; Xinyou hid elite cavalry to charge Qiaohan Mountain and lure them out.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitive rebels raided Santai. Xinyou concealed picked horsemen to strike Qiaohan Mountain and lure the enemy out.

sentences.zh: 伏起，短兵接，斬其酋賽屹塔黑振江。

translations.literal: The ambush rose; at close quarters they engaged and beheaded their chief Saiyitaheizhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush sprang up, and in close fighting they killed the rebel chief Saiyitaheizhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 俄而安酋阿里達什寇邊，從錦棠出屯玉都巴什。

translations.literal: Soon the An chief Alidash raided the border; he followed Jintang to encamp at Yudubashi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the An chief Alidash raided the frontier. Xinyou followed Jintang to encamp at Yudubashi.

sentences.zh: 辛酉率二百騎為前驅，怒馬陷陣，斬執旗賊，奪其旗以歸。

translations.literal: Xinyou led two hundred riders as vanguard, charged furiously into the battle line, beheaded the flag-bearing rebel, and seized the flag to return.
translations.idiomatic: Xinyou led two hundred horsemen as vanguard, charged straight into the enemy line, killed the standard-bearer, and brought back the captured banner.

sentences.zh: 寇大潰，追至畢勒套格，殺其​​黨且盡。

translations.literal: The rebels were greatly routed; pursuing to Biletaoge, their faction was nearly all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke in rout. He pursued to Biletaoge and virtually annihilated their band.

sentences.zh: 西陲告寧，乞歸養。

translations.literal: The western frontier reported tranquility, and he begged to return home to nurse his parents.
translations.idiomatic: When the western frontier was declared at peace, he asked leave to go home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 甲午之役，率師鎮登州，即於軍前授廣西右江鎮，治軍如故。

translations.literal: In the Jiawu campaign he led troops to garrison Dengzhou, and was forthwith at the army front granted the Guangxi Youjiang garrison, governing the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sino-Japanese War of 1894–95 he led troops garrisoning Dengzhou and was promoted on the spot to command the Youjiang garrison in Guangxi, continuing to drill his men as before.

sentences.zh: 尋徙鎮登州。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to garrison Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to command the Dengzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，充武衛軍先鋒左翼長，從李秉衡禦敵，未戰而潰。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, he served as left wing commander of the Wuwei Army vanguard, followed Li Bingheng to resist the enemy, and routed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, he served as left wing commander of the Wuwei vanguard under Li Bingheng. His force collapsed without even giving battle.

sentences.zh: 後除雲南提督，未到官，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed provincial military commander of Yunnan; before reaching office he died, and condolence followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed provincial military commander of Yunnan but died before taking up the post; standard mourning honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 金運昌，字景亭，安徽盱眙人。

translations.literal: Jin Yunchang, style name Jingting, was a native of Xuyi in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yunchang, whose style name was Jingting, came from Xuyi in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少孤，遭寇亂，總兵郭寶昌之母曹氏撫之，從姓郭。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he suffered bandit turmoil; regional commander Guo Baochang's mother Lady Cao raised him, and he took the surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood during the disorders, he was raised by Lady Cao, mother of regional commander Guo Baochang, and took the Guo surname.

sentences.zh: 既長，入貲為守備。

translations.literal: When grown, he purchased entry as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he purchased an appointment as garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 從寶昌徵發、捻，積勳至游擊。

translations.literal: Following Baochang he campaigned against the Fa and Nian, and by accumulated merit rose to mobile corps commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Baochang in campaigns against the Muslim rebels of the northwest and the Nian, rising through merit to mobile corps commander.

sentences.zh: 論河防功，賜號勉勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In reckoning Yellow River defense merit he was granted the title Mianyongbatulu.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on river defense he received the honorific Mianyongbatulu.

sentences.zh: 平畿南，擢總兵，晉勇號鏗僧額。

translations.literal: Pacifying the southern capital region, he was promoted to regional commander and advanced in brave title to Kengsenge.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying the southern capital region he was promoted to regional commander and his honorific was advanced to Kengsenge.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，遷提督，復姓金氏。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified, he was transferred to provincial military commander and restored the surname Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After the western Nian were suppressed he was promoted to provincial military commander and resumed the Jin surname.

sentences.zh: 從寶昌卓勝軍還陝。

translations.literal: He followed Baochang's Zhuosheng Army back to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Shaanxi with Baochang's Zhuosheng Army.

sentences.zh: 同治八年，寶昌創發，運昌代領其眾，調防綏德。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tongzhi, Baochang fell ill; Yunchang took his place leading the masses and was transferred to garrison Suide.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tongzhi, Baochang fell ill and Yunchang took command of his troops, transferring to garrison Suide.

sentences.zh: 時湘軍已剿金積堡，運昌自清澗至，分所部略其西北，毀長牆。

translations.literal: At this time the Hunan Army had already suppressed Jinjibao; Yunchang came from Qingjian, divided his subordinates to raid its northwest, and destroyed the long wall.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan Army was already besieging Jinjibao when Yunchang arrived from Qingjian, sent detachments to probe the northwest, and tore down the long defensive wall.

sentences.zh: 馬化隆勢蹙，遣黨擾北山，冀斷湘軍糧運。

translations.literal: Ma Hualong's situation was pressed; he sent partisans to harass Beishan, hoping to cut the Hunan Army's grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Hualong, hard pressed, sent raiders to trouble Beishan in hopes of cutting the Hunan Army's supply line.

sentences.zh: 一自河西道葉升堡，屬劉松山；

translations.literal: One route from the Hexi road at Yeshengbao, subordinate to Liu Songshan;
translations.idiomatic: One column came down the Hexi route from Yeshengbao under Liu Songshan;

sentences.zh: 一自山西道花定，屬運昌：並達靈州。

translations.literal: one from the Shanxi road at Huading, subordinate to Yunchang: both reached Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: another from the Shanxi road at Huading under Yunchang—both converging on Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 回既陷定邊，運昌所部多南人，雜食青稞、高粱，患腹病。

translations.literal: After the Hui had taken Dingbian, Yunchang's subordinates were mostly southerners, eating barley and sorghum mixed, and suffered belly illness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Muslims seized Dingbian, Yunchang's men—mostly southerners—ate barley and sorghum unfamiliar to them and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠調寶昌來援，以河防不能赴。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang summoned Baochang to come to aid, but because of river defense he could not go.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang called for Baochang to reinforce them, but Baochang could not leave his river-defense post.

sentences.zh: 是時，陝回陳林、禹彥祿等十三營，益以本地土回，號稱十餘萬，卓勝軍孤立其間，幾無日不戰。

translations.literal: At this time the Shaanxi Hui Chen Lin, Yu Yanlu, and thirteen other battalions, further joined by local native Hui, claimed more than one hundred thousand; the Zhuosheng Army was isolated among them, and there was scarcely a day without battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi Muslim chiefs Chen Lin and Yu Yanlu commanded thirteen battalions, reinforced by local Hui, claiming more than one hundred thousand men. The Zhuosheng Army stood isolated among them and fought nearly every day.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，軍益飢疲，至殺馬為食。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the army grew ever hungrier and wearier, until they killed horses for food.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year hunger and exhaustion worsened until the troops were reduced to slaughtering their horses for food.

sentences.zh: 回且決渠灌我壘，會風濤大作，運昌晝夜立水中，激厲將士，列椿囊土御之，回不得逞。

translations.literal: The Hui moreover breached the canal to flood our ramparts; it happened that wind and waves surged greatly; Yunchang day and night stood in the water, rousing officers and soldiers, arranging stakes and bagging earth to defend against it, and the Hui could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also breached the canal to flood the Qing ramparts. When wind and waves rose furiously, Yunchang stood in the water day and night to hearten his men, driving in stakes and piling sandbags to hold the water back, and the rebels failed in the attempt.

sentences.zh: 適劉錦棠等越渠橫出，回大潰。

translations.literal: Just then Liu Jintang and others crossed the canal and burst out transversely; the Hui routed in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment Liu Jintang led troops across the canal in a flank attack and the rebels collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 因議夾河築壘護餉道，兩日壘成，回至，運昌戰卻之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they discussed building ramparts along both sides of the river to protect the supply route; in two days the ramparts were completed; when the Hui came, Yunchang fought and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: They then decided to build fortifications on both banks to secure the supply line. The works were finished in two days, and when rebels attacked Yunchang drove them back.

sentences.zh: 湘軍開溝築堤以防水，運昌壁近棗園。

translations.literal: The Hunan Army opened ditches and built dikes to guard against water; Yunchang's fortifications were near Zaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Hunan Army dug channels and raised dikes against flooding while Yunchang stationed his camp near Zaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 冰忽解，回乃憑秦渠設卡，運昌越渠擊之，回收入堡。

translations.literal: Suddenly the ice broke; the Hui then relied on the Qin Canal to set up checkpoints; Yunchang crossed the canal to strike them, and the Hui withdrew into the fort.
translations.idiomatic: When the ice broke suddenly the rebels established blocking posts along the Qin Canal. Yunchang crossed the canal to attack and drove them back into their fort.

sentences.zh: 越二日，堡回悉眾出，騎寇趨板橋，步寇決渠水南下。

translations.literal: After two days, the fort Hui with their entire force came out; cavalry raided toward Banqiao; infantry raiders breached the canal water and went south.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later the entire garrison sallied out: cavalry struck toward Banqiao while infantry broke the canal and flooded the area to the south.

sentences.zh: 運昌軍阻水，錦棠分三路泅水與合，並力轟潰其眾。

translations.literal: Yunchang's army was blocked by water; Jintang divided into three routes and swam through water to join him, and with combined strength cannonaded and routed their masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang's force was cut off by the floodwaters until Jintang split his men into three columns that swam across to join him; together they battered the rebel host into flight.

sentences.zh: 未幾，回復運磚石築卡於北，環以長堤，欲引馬連水以困我。

translations.literal: Before long, the Hui again transported bricks and stone to build checkpoints in the north, ringed by a long dike, intending to draw horses and connect water to distress us.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels hauled brick and stone northward to build new posts ringed by a long dike, aiming to divert the river and hem the Qing forces in with water.

sentences.zh: 運昌亟令軍士攜鋤錨，夷其卡而還。

translations.literal: Yunchang urgently ordered soldiers to carry hoes and anchors, level their checkpoints, and return.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang promptly sent troops with picks and mattocks to tear down the posts and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 四月，陳林率眾出花定掠食。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Chen Lin led the masses out from Huading to plunder food.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Chen Lin led his men out from Huading to raid for grain.

sentences.zh: 運昌使提督王鳳鳴御之，敗之磚井鎮。

translations.literal: Yunchang sent provincial military commander Wang Fengming to resist them, and defeated them at Zhuanjing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang sent provincial military commander Wang Fengming to intercept them and defeated them at Zhuanjing.

sentences.zh: 同時葉升堡道亦通，軍威復振。

translations.literal: At the same time the Yeshengbao road also opened, and army prestige revived.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time the route through Yeshengbao reopened and army morale recovered.

sentences.zh: 七月，克馬家兩寨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, they captured the two stockades of the Ma family.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month they took the two Ma family stockades.

sentences.zh: 值新麥熟，運昌與錦棠分刈，並糜粟割之。

translations.literal: It happened that new wheat ripened; Yunchang and Jintang divided reaping, and also reaped broomcorn millet and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The new wheat ripened, and Yunchang and Jintang divided the harvest, reaping broomcorn millet and grain as well.

sentences.zh: 回來爭，輒敗走。

translations.literal: When the Hui came to contest, they were at once defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever rebels came to contest the harvest they were beaten back in flight.

sentences.zh: 遂築壘蔡家橋。

translations.literal: Thereupon they built ramparts at Caijia Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: They then fortified Caijia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 橋跨秦渠，內設卡，外障水，馬化隆前所為阻遏官軍者也。

translations.literal: The bridge spanned the Qin Canal, with checkpoints set within and water barred without—the obstruction Ma Hualong had earlier made to hinder the government army.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge crossed the Qin Canal with inner checkpoints and outer water barriers—the very choke point Ma Hualong had used to block government troops.

sentences.zh: 至是決水反灌，破壘三、卡十有一，乘勢下秦壩關，逼東關。

translations.literal: At this time they breached water to flow back and irrigate, broke three ramparts and eleven checkpoints, took advantage of momentum to descend Qinba Pass, and pressed Dong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They now turned the water back on the rebels, destroying three forts and eleven posts, then pressed through Qinba Pass to threaten Dong Pass.

sentences.zh: 議掘壕築牆久困之，與錦棠分段興工。

translations.literal: They discussed digging trenches and building walls to wear them down over time; with Jintang they divided sections to begin work.
translations.idiomatic: They planned to dig trenches and build walls for a protracted siege, and Yunchang and Jintang divided the work into sections.

sentences.zh: 三日畢乃事，遣兵分守之，遂合金積圍。

translations.literal: In three days the work was finished; they sent troops to garrison in divided posts, and then joined the Jinjibao encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The works were finished in three days; garrisons were posted along them, and the line was linked to the siege ring around Jinjibao.

sentences.zh: 日咯血數次，戰不少休。

translations.literal: Daily he expectorated blood several times, yet in battle he did not slack at all.
translations.idiomatic: He spat blood several times a day, yet never slackened in combat.

sentences.zh: 陳林降，運昌以西林、河州未下，宜稍示寬大。

translations.literal: Chen Lin surrendered; Yunchang because Xilin and Hezhou were not yet taken, deemed it appropriate to show a little leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Lin surrendered, Yunchang argued that because Xilin and Hezhou had not yet fallen the policy should be somewhat lenient.

sentences.zh: 強者編籍，弱者就糧，群回多乞款。

translations.literal: The strong were enrolled in registers, the weak accepted grain; many Hui groups begged for terms.
translations.idiomatic: Strong fighters were registered for service while weaker men were put on government rations, and many rebel bands petitioned to surrender.

sentences.zh: 馬化隆勢蹙，亦束首歸命。

translations.literal: Ma Hualong's situation was pressed; he also bound his head and submitted to fate.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Hualong, hard pressed, also bowed his head in submission.

sentences.zh: 於是寧、靈悉定，論功賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ning and Ling were all pacified; in reckoning merit he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia and Lingzhou were then fully secured, and for his merit he was awarded an imperial yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 駐纏金，平甘回馬勝福亂，晉頭品服。

translations.literal: Stationed at Chanjin, he pacified the Gansu Hui Ma Shengfu's turmoil, and was advanced to first-grade court dress.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Chanjin, suppressed the Gansu Muslim rebellion led by Ma Shengfu, and was promoted to first-grade court dress.

sentences.zh: 徙駐包頭，數請於宗棠，願西征。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Baotou, he repeatedly petitioned Zongtang, wishing to campaign west.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Baotou, he repeatedly petitioned Zuo Zongtang for permission to join the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，宗棠請敕淮勇出關助剿，報可。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, Zongtang requested imperial edict for Huai Army braves to exit the pass to aid suppression; the reply granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu, Zuo Zongtang secured imperial approval to send Huai Army troops beyond the pass to reinforce the campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，行抵烏魯木齊，命署提督，越二年，實授。

translations.literal: The next year in summer, traveling he reached Wulumuqi, was ordered to act as provincial military commander; after two years, received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he reached Ürümqi and was appointed acting provincial military commander; two years later he received the full commission.

sentences.zh: 口外經喪亂後，戶口減耗。

translations.literal: Beyond the pass, after suffering disorder, household registers were reduced and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the pass the population had been drastically reduced by years of turmoil.

sentences.zh: 運昌興水利，課農桑，建橋樑，皆割俸自任之。

translations.literal: Yunchang promoted waterworks, assessed farming and sericulture, built bridges—all by cutting his salary to undertake himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang promoted irrigation, encouraged farming and sericulture, and built bridges, paying for it all out of his own salary.

sentences.zh: 其斥巨款賑畿菑，實秉義母郭曹氏命。

translations.literal: His expending great funds to relieve famine in the capital region truly followed his adoptive mother Lady Guo Cao's command.
translations.idiomatic: His large donations to relieve famine around the capital were made at the bidding of his adoptive mother, Lady Cao of the Guo family.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章為請於朝，特建坊旌異之。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang pleaded on her behalf at court; a special arch was built to mark her distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized the court on her behalf, and a commemorative arch was erected in her honor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he resigned citing illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，卹如製，入祀卓勝軍昭忠祠。

translations.literal: After a year he died; condolence followed regulations; he entered sacrifice in the Zhuosheng Army Loyal-and-Martyred Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year; standard mourning honors were granted, and he was enshrined in the Zhuosheng Army Martyrs' Temple.

sentences.zh: 妾王氏、馬氏、張氏，先後仰藥殉節，皆獲旌。

translations.literal: Concubines Lady Wang, Lady Ma, and Lady Zhang, successively took poison by mouth and died for integrity; all received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His concubines Lady Wang, Lady Ma, and Lady Zhang successively took poison to follow him in death, and all were posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 黃萬鵬，字搏九，湖南寧鄉人，本籍善化。

translations.literal: Huang Wanpeng, style name Bojiu, was a native of Ningxiang in Hunan; his original register was Shanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wanpeng, whose style name was Bojiu, came from Ningxiang in Hunan, though his household register stood in Shanhua.

sentences.zh: 初從曾國荃援贛、皖，積勳至都司。

translations.literal: At first he followed Zeng Guoquan to aid Jiangxi and Anhui, and by accumulated merit rose to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Zeng Guoquan in Jiangxi and Anhui, rising through merit to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 從克江寧，歷遷總兵，賜號力勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Jiangning, he was promoted through ranks to regional commander, and granted the title Liyongbatulu.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Nanjing he rose to regional commander and received the honorific Liyongbatulu.

sentences.zh: 捻入鄂，犯德安，萬鵬馳救，大敗之，又破之安陸。

translations.literal: The Nian entered Hubei and attacked De'an; Wanpeng rushed to rescue, routed them greatly, and again defeated them at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian invaded Hubei and struck De'an, Wanpeng rushed to the rescue and routed them, then defeated them again at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 會師新洲，於是夾擊，大破虜，擢提督。

translations.literal: Joining forces at Xinzhou, thereupon with pincer attack they routed the enemy greatly, and he was promoted to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Allied with other forces at Xinzhou, he caught the rebels in a pincer and crushed them, earning promotion to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠西征，調赴陝，署漢中鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Zuo Zongtang campaigned west, he was transferred to Shaanxi and acted as regional commander of Hanzhong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo Zongtang launched the western campaign Wanpeng was transferred to Shaanxi as acting commander of the Hanzhong garrison.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，從攻西寧，抵碾伯，戰硤口，回潰走，圍解。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi, following the attack on Xining, he reached Nianbo, fought at Xiakou; the Hui routed and fled, and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he joined the assault on Xining, reached Nianbo, and fought at Xiakou; the rebels fled in rout and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 明年，從劉錦棠克向陽堡，進圍大通，降之。

translations.literal: The next year, following Liu Jintang he captured Xiangyang Fort, advanced to besiege Datong, and it surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, with Liu Jintang, he took Xiangyang Fort, advanced to besiege Datong, and secured its surrender.

sentences.zh: 選降眾立旌善五旗，馬隊屬萬鵬領之，隨攻肅州。

translations.literal: Selected among surrendered masses they established the Jingshan Five Banners; the cavalry was subordinate to Wanpeng's leadership, and followed to attack Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From among the surrendered rebels he organized the Jingshan Five Banners cavalry under Wanpeng's command and marched on Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 事寧，賜頭品服。

translations.literal: When affairs were pacified, he was granted first-grade court dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was granted first-grade court dress.

sentences.zh: 十三年，河州閃殿臣复叛，萬鵬率崔偉等進擊，敗之城南二十里鋪。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Hezhou's Shan Dian-chen rebelled again; Wanpeng led Cui Wei and others in forward attack, and defeated him at the twenty-li post south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Shan Dian-chen rebelled again at Hezhou; Wanpeng led Cui Wei and others against him and defeated him at a post twenty li south of the city.

sentences.zh: 寇竄賈家集，官軍攻弗克，萬鵬從姚家嶺馳下合攻，燔其堡，更勇號為伯奇。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Jiajiaji; the government army attacked but could not overcome; Wanpeng from Yaojialing galloped down to join attack, burned their fort, and his brave title was changed to Boqi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Jiajiaji where government troops failed to dislodge them until Wanpeng galloped down from Yaojialing in a combined assault that burned their fort; his honorific was then advanced to Boqi.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，出關。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he exited the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he crossed beyond the pass into the west.

sentences.zh: 時土回馬明據古牧，白彥虎聞官軍至，自紅廟子與合師，夜襲黃田。

translations.literal: At this time the native Hui Ma Ming held Gumux; Bai Yanhu hearing the government army had come, from Hongmiao joined forces, and by night raided Huangtian.
translations.idiomatic: The local Muslim chief Ma Ming held Gumux; when Bai Yanhu heard government troops were approaching he marched from Hongmiao to join him and they launched a night assault on Huangtian.

sentences.zh: 旦日，聞古牧角聲起，萬鵬與餘虎恩馳擊寇騎卻之，語詳餘虎恩傳。

translations.literal: At dawn, hearing Gumux signal horns arise, Wanpeng and Yu Hu'en galloped to strike the bandit cavalry and repelled them—the account is detailed in Yu Hu'en's biography.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak, when signal horns sounded at Gumux, Wanpeng and Yu Hu'en galloped out and drove the rebel cavalry back; the full account appears in Yu Hu'en's biography.

sentences.zh: 烏魯木齊諸城既复，追至池墩而還。

translations.literal: After the cities of Wulumuqi were recovered, he pursued to Chidun and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ürümqi cities were recovered he pursued as far as Chidun and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 捷入，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Victory was reported in; he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory reached the court he was awarded an imperial yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 北路略定，逸寇多亡匿東南山谷。

translations.literal: The northern route was roughly pacified; fleeing bandits mostly hid in southeast mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: As the northern route was largely secured, fugitive rebels hid in the valleys of the southeastern hills.

sentences.zh: 萬鵬復與虎恩取道大小鹽池墩至柴窩，略有斬擒。

translations.literal: Wanpeng again with Hu'en took the route from Great and Small Yan Chi Forts to Chaiwo, and had some beheadings and captures.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng and Yu Hu'en again swept from the Great and Small Salt Pond Forts to Chaiwo, killing and capturing a number of rebels.

sentences.zh: 八月，金順攻瑪納斯南城弗勝，錦棠檄萬鵬助擊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Jin Shun attacked the southern city of Manasi without victory; Jintang dispatched Wanpeng to aid the attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Jin Shun's assault on the southern city of Manas stalled, and Jintang ordered Wanpeng to reinforce the attack.

sentences.zh: 掘隧以攻，寇死拒，矢貫萬鵬臂，拔之，更疾戰，與諸軍大破之。

translations.literal: Digging tunnels to attack, the bandits resisted to the death; an arrow pierced Wanpeng's arm; he pulled it out and fought all the more fiercely; with the various armies they routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They dug siege tunnels to assault the city; the defenders resisted to the last. An arrow pierced Wanpeng's arm; he pulled it out and fought on all the harder until allied forces broke the city in a great victory.

sentences.zh: 三年，攻克達坂，乘勝取托克遜。

translations.literal: In the third year, they captured Daban; riding victory they took Tuokexun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they took Dabancheng and pressed on to capture Turpan.

sentences.zh: 至小草湖，遇伏，圍萬鵬數匝。

translations.literal: Reaching Xiaocaohu, they met an ambush; Wanpeng was surrounded several circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaocaohu they ran into an ambush that surrounded Wanpeng several times over.

sentences.zh: 萬鵬率隊盪決，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Wanpeng led his detachment in a charging breakthrough; wherever he went none could stand.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng led a desperate charge that broke the encirclement and swept all before him.

sentences.zh: 錦棠軍繼至，寇大潰，詔予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Jintang's army followed and arrived; the bandits routed greatly; an edict granted Yunqiwei hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintang's reinforcements arrived the rebels collapsed in rout, and the court granted Wanpeng the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 是役，帕夏知不免，飲藥死，彥虎遂奔開都河西岸。

translations.literal: In this campaign, the Pasha knew he could not escape, drank medicine and died; Yanhu then fled to the west bank of the Kaidu River.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign the Atalik Yaqub Beg, seeing escape impossible, took poison and died, and Bai Yanhu fled to the west bank of the Kaidu River.

sentences.zh: 七月。

translations.literal: Seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month,

sentences.zh: 師至曲惠，錦棠自向開都河，而令萬鵬道烏沙塔拉傍博斯騰淖爾西行，出庫爾勒之背。

translations.literal: The army reached Quhui; Jintang himself turned toward the Kaidu River, while ordering Wanpeng by the route Wushatala along Bosten Lake to go west, emerging behind Korla.
translations.idiomatic: the army reached Quhui. Jintang marched on the Kaidu River himself while directing Wanpeng west along Lake Bosten via Wushatala to strike Korla from the rear.

sentences.zh: 彥虎懾軍威，已先期遁。

translations.literal: Yanhu feared army prestige and had already fled ahead of time.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanhu, overawed by government strength, had already fled beforehand.

sentences.zh: 诇知脅纏回走布古爾，亟​​行四百里追及之，戰良久，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Scout intelligence knew he coerced loyalist Hui to flee toward Bugur; urgently traveling four hundred li he overtook them, battled long, and routed their masses greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that he was driving loyalist Muslims toward Bugur, Wanpeng marched four hundred li in haste, overtook them after a long fight, and inflicted a heavy defeat.

sentences.zh: 九月，馳抵托和奈，再敗之，收庫車，進駐拜城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, galloping he reached Tuohenai, again defeated them, recovered Kuche, and advanced to garrison at Baicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he rushed to Tuohenai, defeated the rebels again, recovered Kucha, and advanced to garrison Baicheng.

sentences.zh: 履冰夜行至銅廠，諸軍直搏之，寇愕走。

translations.literal: Treading ice he traveled by night to Tongchang; the various armies straightway grappled them; the bandits fled in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Marching over ice by night to Tongchang, his troops struck head-on and the startled rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 萬鵬長驅察爾齊克台西，斬數千級。

translations.literal: Wanpeng long-drove west of Cha'erqi Fort, beheading several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng drove west of Cha'erqi Station and took several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 越二日，夜抵扎木台稍憩，即引兵阿克蘇城。

translations.literal: After two days, by night reaching Zhamutai he rested briefly, then led troops to Akesu city.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he reached Zhamutai by night for a brief rest, then marched on Aksu.

sentences.zh: 未至城數里，見西南塵埃坌起，會諜報彥虎走烏什，嗾安集延走葉爾羌纟圭追師。

translations.literal: Before reaching the city by several li, he saw southwest dust rise in a mass; it happened that spies reported Yanhu fled toward Wushi, incited Kokand to flee toward Yarkand, and the pursuing army was already closing in.
translations.idiomatic: Several li short of the city he saw dust rising to the southwest; scouts reported that Bai Yanhu had fled toward Wushi, had incited Kokand troops toward Yarkand, and that a pursuit column was already bearing down.

sentences.zh: 錦棠乃舍安夷，而令萬鵬專追彥虎，阻河漲不能濟。

translations.literal: Jintang thereupon set aside the An Yi, and ordered Wanpeng exclusively to pursue Yanhu; blocked by the river's rise he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jintang then set aside the An Yi rebels and ordered Wanpeng to pursue Bai Yanhu alone, but the swollen river could not be crossed.

sentences.zh: 時彥虎止隔河十里許造飯，掩襲可擒也，而我師遽返，錦棠大怒，責令復進。

translations.literal: At this time Yanhu was only separated by the river by about ten li making food; a concealed assault could have captured him, yet our army abruptly returned; Jintang was greatly angry and ordered him to advance again.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanhu was then only about ten li across the river cooking his meal—a surprise attack could have taken him—but our troops turned back abruptly. Jintang was furious and ordered Wanpeng to advance again.

sentences.zh: 於是萬鵬渡胡馬納克河，行戈壁八十里，獲其後隊馬有才，進拔烏什，而彥虎已走喀什矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wanpeng crossed the Humana River, traveled the Gobi eighty li, captured his rear detachment Ma Youcai, advanced and took Wushi, while Yanhu had already fled to Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng then crossed the Humana River, marched eighty li across the Gobi, captured the rear guard commander Ma Youcai, and took Wushi—but Bai Yanhu had already fled to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 東四城俱下，詔改騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: The four eastern cities were all taken; an edict changed his office to Qiduwei hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: With the four eastern cities all secured, the court advanced his hereditary rank to Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 當是時，伯克胡里據喀什攻漢城，彥虎至，助之，勢益張。

translations.literal: At this time Bek Huli held Kashgar attacking the Han city; Yanhu arrived and aided him, and momentum grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bek Huli held Kashgar and was assaulting the Chinese quarter; when Bai Yanhu arrived to reinforce him their strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 守備何步雲告急，錦棠檄萬鵬道布魯特與虎恩期會喀城。

translations.literal: Garrison commander He Buyun reported urgency; Jintang dispatched Wanpeng by the Burut route to meet Hu'en by appointment at Kashgar city.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander He Buyun sent an urgent appeal for help; Jintang ordered Wanpeng to march by the Burut route and rendezvous with Yu Hu'en at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 萬鵬倍道應赴，緣雪山千餘裡，每以毯鋪地濟師。

translations.literal: Wanpeng doubled his route to respond; along snowy mountains for more than a thousand li, each time spreading blankets on the ground to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng hurried to answer the call, marching more than a thousand li along snow-covered mountains and laying down blankets at every step to ease the troops' passage.

sentences.zh: 十一月，抵城北麻古木，虎恩亦抵城東牌素特。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he reached Magumu north of the city; Hu'en also reached Paisute east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reached Magumu north of the city while Yu Hu'en arrived at Paisute on the east.

sentences.zh: 寇诇騎馳歸，曰：「大軍至矣！

translations.literal: The bandits' scout riders galloped back, saying: "The great army has arrived!
translations.idiomatic: Enemy scouts came galloping back with word: "The main force is upon us!

sentences.zh: 」於是二巨酋走回城北，進搗之，則又宵遁。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the two great chieftains fled back to north of the city; advancing to strike them, they again fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: " At that the two rebel chieftains retreated north of the city; when he pressed the attack, they fled again under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 萬鵬向西北追彥虎，至爰岌槽，與賊後隊遇，生擒偽元帥馬元，斬其副白彥龍。

translations.literal: Wanpeng pursued Yanhu northwest to Ai'ji Cao, met the bandits' rear guard, captured alive the false commander-in-chief Ma Yuan, and beheaded his lieutenant Bai Yanlong.
translations.idiomatic: Wanpeng drove northwest after Bai Yanhu to Ai'ji Cao, met the rebel rear guard, took the false commander-in-chief Ma Yuan alive, and slew his lieutenant Bai Yanlong.

sentences.zh: 次日，追至恰哈瑪納，為布魯特人所阻，彥虎遂奔俄。

translations.literal: The next day, pursuing to Qiahamana, he was blocked by Buruts; Yanhu then fled to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pursued as far as Qiahamana, but Burut tribesmen barred his path, and Bai Yanhu escaped into Russia.

sentences.zh: 新疆平，改授二等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: Xinjiang was pacified; he was transferred to Second-class Light Chariot Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: With Xinjiang pacified, the court advanced him to Second-class Light Chariot Commandant.

sentences.zh: 四年，凱旋，乞歸省。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he returned in triumph and requested leave to visit home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he returned in triumph and asked leave to visit his family.

sentences.zh: 越二年，仍赴新疆治軍。

translations.literal: After two years he again went to Xinjiang to manage the army.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he returned to Xinjiang to take charge of the troops.

sentences.zh: 南北山邊防敉平，晉頭品秩。

translations.literal: The northern and southern mountain frontier defenses were pacified; he was promoted to first-rank grade.
translations.idiomatic: With the northern and southern mountain frontiers pacified, he was promoted to first-rank grade.

sentences.zh: 歷權喀什回城協副將，阿克蘇、巴里坤各鎮總兵，新疆提督。

translations.literal: He successively held acting posts as Kashgar Hui-city assistant deputy commander, garrison commander at Aksu and Barkol, and military governor of Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as acting assistant deputy commander of the Kashgar Muslim quarter, garrison commander at Aksu and Barkol, and military governor of Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 又襲其叔登和世職，並為二等男爵。

translations.literal: He also inherited his uncle Dengho's hereditary office and was made a second-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He also inherited his uncle Dengho's hereditary post and was created a second-class baron.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徵入京，創發，卒於道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital, fell ill en route, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was summoned to the capital, took ill on the journey, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 予建祠。

translations.literal: A memorial shrine was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him a memorial shrine.

sentences.zh: 子鉞，道員，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yue, a circuit intendant, inherited the peerage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yue, a circuit intendant, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 餘虎恩，湖南平江人。

translations.literal: Yu Hu'en was a native of Pingjiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hu'en came from Pingjiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，喜讀書。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth and raised in poverty, he nevertheless loved books.

sentences.zh: 初從曾國籓討粵寇，積勳至副將。

translations.literal: At first he followed Zeng Guofan against the Cantonese rebels, accumulating merit until deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Zeng Guofan against the Taiping rebels and rose through merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，從劉松山徵捻，蹙之沙河西，擢總兵，賜號精勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi he followed Liu Songshan against the Nian, pressing them west of the Sha River; he was promoted to brigade commander and granted the title Valiant Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi era he campaigned under Liu Songshan against the Nian, driving them west of the Sha River; he was promoted to brigade commander and granted the title Valiant Baturu.

sentences.zh: 張總愚與回匪合，攻破金谷、銀渠，又敗之郿縣，晉提督。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu joined with Muslim bandits, took Jingu and Yinqu; he was again defeated at Mei County and Hu'en was promoted to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu allied with Muslim rebels and seized Jingu and Yinqu, Hu'en defeated him again at Mei County and was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 寇自宜川渡河，陷山西州縣，又從劉軍追復之，易勇號奇車博。

translations.literal: The bandits crossed the river at Yichuan and seized Shanxi prefectures and counties; he again followed Liu's army to recover them and received the changed brave title Qichebo.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels crossed at Yichuan and overran counties in Shanxi, he followed Liu's army in the recovery and received the new brave title Qichebo.

sentences.zh: 軍獲鹿，適郭松林被圍，虎恩銳身馳救，圍解。

translations.literal: The army reached Luquan; just then Guo Songlin was besieged—Hu'en dashed boldly to rescue and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: At Luquan, when Guo Songlin was surrounded, Hu'en charged in person to the rescue and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 繞道長驅，騎寇雖猋騁，遇戰輒披靡。

translations.literal: Taking a roundabout route in long drive, though mounted bandits raced like wind, whenever battle was joined they collapsed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Marching by a roundabout route, he met mounted rebels racing like storm-wind; yet whenever he gave battle they broke at once.

sentences.zh: 上念陝事棘，命左宗棠舉將才，乃薦松山部將尤異者十數人，虎恩與焉，寵以頭品服，令赴陝軍。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful that Shaanxi affairs were thorny, ordered Zuo Zongtang to recommend military talent; he then recommended more than ten outstanding generals from Songshan's command, Hu'en among them; favored with first-rank uniform, ordered to proceed to the Shaanxi army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, troubled by the crisis in Shaanxi, ordered Zuo Zongtang to name able commanders; Zuo recommended more than a dozen outstanding officers from Liu Songshan's command, Hu'en among them, honored with first-rank insignia and sent to the Shaanxi front.

sentences.zh: 靈州既克，松山進兵板橋、蔡家橋。

translations.literal: Once Lingzhou was taken, Songshan advanced to Banqiao and Caijiaqiao.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingzhou fell, Songshan advanced on Banqiao and Caijiaqiao.

sentences.zh: 有頃，回敗走，虎恩騎旅突之，驟若風雨，回不得歸，下其村寨三十餘。

translations.literal: Before long the Hui were defeated and fled; Hu'en's cavalry brigade rushed upon them sudden as wind and rain; the Hui could not return; he took more than thirty of their stockades and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Muslims were routed in flight; Hu'en's cavalry struck like a sudden storm, cut off their retreat, and captured more than thirty stockades and villages.

sentences.zh: 金積平，假歸。

translations.literal: Jinji was pacified; he took temporary leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinji was pacified he took temporary leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，命募軍赴甘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was ordered to recruit troops and proceed to Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was ordered to raise troops and march to Gansu.

sentences.zh: 劉錦棠攻西寧，虎恩率軍至陝口，週覽形勢。

translations.literal: Liu Jintang attacked Xining; Hu'en led his army to Shankou and surveyed the terrain all around.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jintang attacked Xining, Hu'en led his force to Shankou and reconnoitered the ground on every side.

sentences.zh: 寇出拒，被困，卒擊卻之。

translations.literal: Bandits came out to resist; he was trapped but finally drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels came out to resist; though briefly trapped, he at last drove them back.

sentences.zh: 錦棠覘回勢盛，赴平戎驛造橋濟湟，自督師築壘北岸，令虎恩築南岸。

translations.literal: Jintang observed the Hui position strong; he went to Pingyi Post to build a bridge to cross the Huang River; personally supervised troops building ramparts on the north bank and ordered Hu'en to build on the south bank.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Muslim position still strong, Jintang went to Pingyi Post to bridge the Huang River, supervised fortifications on the north bank himself, and ordered Hu'en to entrench the south bank.

sentences.zh: 未成，馬營灣寇突至，虎恩轟擊之，錦棠亦敗湟北寇，於是西寧告寧。

translations.literal: Before completion, bandits at Mayingwan suddenly arrived; Hu'en bombarded them; Jintang also defeated Huang River north bandits; thus Xining was reported peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Before the works were finished rebels at Mayingwan struck suddenly; Hu'en blasted them back while Jintang defeated the enemy north of the river, and Xining was declared secure.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: For merit he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 隨攻肅州，軍南門，與諸將討平之，除陝安鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Suzhou, army at south gate, with various generals pacified it; appointed commander of Shen'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Suzhou at the south gate and, with the other commanders, brought the city to submission; he was then appointed garrison commander of Shen'an.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，從出關。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he followed the army out of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he marched west beyond the frontier pass.

sentences.zh: 宗棠慮戈壁糧運艱阻，虎恩請身任之，乃絕幕而西。

translations.literal: Zongtang worried Gobi grain transport was difficult and obstructed; Hu'en requested to bear it personally himself; thereupon he crossed the desert westward.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang feared that grain convoys across the Gobi would prove impossible; Hu'en volunteered to take charge himself and marched west across the desert.

sentences.zh: 抵哈密，取餘糧，逾天山，遞送巴里坤古城。

translations.literal: He reached Hami, took surplus grain, crossed the Tianshan, and relay-delivered it to Barkol old city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Hami, gathered surplus grain, crossed the Tianshan, and relayed supplies to the old city at Barkol.

sentences.zh: 邊既實，襲黃田，破其卡。

translations.literal: Once the border was solid, he raided Huangtian and broke their pass-station.
translations.idiomatic: With the frontier provisioned, he struck Huangtian and destroyed its outpost.

sentences.zh: 忽古牧寇壓師而陣，虎恩亟自山馳下，與寇騎戰良久，會董福祥軍助擊中路，寇大潰，遂合圍。

translations.literal: At Hugu Gu the bandits pressed the army into formation; Hu'en urgently galloped down from the mountain, fought the mounted bandits long; Dong Fuxiang's army met to assist striking the center road; the bandits routed greatly; then the encirclement closed.
translations.idiomatic: At Hugu Gu the rebels massed against his column; Hu'en galloped down from the heights and fought their cavalry for a long while until Dong Fuxiang's troops joined the assault on the center; the enemy collapsed in rout and the encirclement was completed.

sentences.zh: 帕夏遣悍黨來援，虎恩率騎旅列山岡，嚴陣以待。

translations.literal: The Pasha sent fierce partisans to aid; Hu'en led the cavalry brigade arrayed on the mountain ridge in strict formation awaiting them.
translations.idiomatic: The Atalik sent fierce reinforcements; Hu'en drew up his cavalry on the ridge in battle order and waited.

sentences.zh: 复麾軍截其歸路，斬關直入，城拔。

translations.literal: Again he commanded the army to cut their return route, sliced through the pass straight in, and the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: He then wheeled his troops to cut off their retreat, stormed the pass, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 度烏垣，寇且他遁，以次下烏魯木齊、迪化及偽王城，予雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: Crossing Wuyuan, the bandits about to flee elsewhere, in sequence he took Urumqi, Dihua, and the false king's city; he was granted Cloud Cavalry Captain hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Wuyuan as the rebels prepared to scatter, he took Urumqi, Dihua, and the rebel capital in succession and was granted the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 明年，踰嶺而南，從錦棠趨柴窩，去達坂二十里。

translations.literal: The next year, crossing the ridge southward, he followed Jintang toward Chaiwo, twenty li from Daban.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he crossed the mountains to the south, followed Jintang toward Chaiwo, and halted twenty li from Daban.

sentences.zh: 夜初鼓，虎恩率騎旅九營，銜枚疾走。

translations.literal: At the first night drum, Hu'en led nine cavalry battalions, gags in mouths, marching swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: At the first night watch Hu'en led nine cavalry battalions forward in silence at forced march.

sentences.zh: 大通哈引湖水衛城，泥深及骭。

translations.literal: Datong Ha drew lake water to guard the city; mud was deep to the shins.
translations.idiomatic: Datong Ha had been flooded to defend the town, and the mud came to a man's shins.

sentences.zh: 虎恩所部掠淖進，依山為陣，斬寇諜十餘騎，回方臥，未覺也，平旦始大驚，悉眾出，據險轟拒。

translations.literal: Hu'en's detachment skimmed the marsh to advance, arrayed along the mountain; beheaded more than ten mounted bandit spies; the Hui side still lay asleep and had not noticed; at daybreak they were greatly startled, all masses came out, held dangerous ground and bombarded in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'en's men skirted the marsh and formed along the hills, cutting down more than a dozen rebel scouts; the garrison still slept unaware until dawn, when they woke in alarm, poured out in full strength, and held the heights under heavy fire.

sentences.zh: 師屹立不動，海古拉援至，虎恩又截之隘口，援騎返奔，追逐數里，斬百餘級。

translations.literal: The army stood firm unmoving; Haigula reinforcements arrived; Hu'en again intercepted them at the pass mouth; the relief cavalry turned and fled; pursued several li and beheaded more than a hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: His troops held their ground; when Haigula's relief column arrived Hu'en blocked the pass, turned the reinforcements back in flight, pursued several li, and took more than a hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 虎恩策城回盼援不至，必遁，預隱兵以待，寇出悉就擒。

translations.literal: Hu'en calculated that the city Hui, seeing aid not arrive, would surely flee; he pre-positioned hidden troops to await them; when the bandits came out all were captured.
