translations.idiomatic: Hu'en judged that the garrison, seeing no relief come, would try to escape; he hid troops along the route, and when the rebels sallied forth they were all taken.

sentences.zh: 達坂复，乘勢下托克遜，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Daban was recovered; riding momentum he took Toksun; he was granted Cavalry Commandant hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Daban was recovered and, pressing the advantage, he took Toksun; the court granted him the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 踰月，規南路，師次曲惠，虎恩取道烏沙塔拉入庫爾勒城，地闃無人，食且盡，乃掘窖糧數万石濟師。

translations.literal: After a month, planning the southern road, the army halted at Quhui; Hu'en took the route Wushatala into Korla city; the land was desolate without people, food nearly exhausted; thereupon he dug cellar grain of tens of thousands of shi to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, campaigning on the southern route, the army halted at Quhui; Hu'en entered Korla by way of Wushatala, found the district deserted and rations nearly gone, and unearthed tens of thousands of shi of buried grain to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 遂與諸將下庫車，凡六日馳九百里。

translations.literal: Thereupon with the various generals he took Kuche; in all six days galloping nine hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the other commanders in taking Kucha after six days' forced march covering nine hundred li.

sentences.zh: 已而喀什噶爾告急，錦棠令虎恩自巴爾楚取中路為正兵，黃萬鵬自烏什道布魯特為奇兵，仍歸虎恩節度。

translations.literal: Before long Kashgar reported urgency; Jintang ordered Hu'en from Barkol by the middle route as main force, Huang Wanpeng from Wushi by the Burut route as flanking force, still under Hu'en's command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kashgar sent urgent appeals; Jintang ordered Hu'en to advance from Barkol on the central route as the main column and Huang Wanpeng from Wushi by the Burut road as the flanking force, both still under Hu'en's command.

sentences.zh: 師抵巴爾楚，會天寒，冰雪凝冽，而喀城警報且日至。

translations.literal: The army reached Barkol; it happened the weather was cold, ice and snow frozen sharp, while Kashgar alarms arrived day by day.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Barkol in bitter cold with ice frozen hard, even as alarms from Kashgar arrived day after day.

sentences.zh: 乃兼程應赴，軍士人人自奮，各以俘白酋取首功為利。

translations.literal: Thereupon he doubled the route to respond; soldiers each roused themselves, each taking capture of white chieftains for first merit as profit.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward at forced march; every soldier roused himself, each hoping to win top credit by capturing a rebel chieftain.

sentences.zh: 日中，虎恩至城東牌素特，夜半時抵喀什漢城下，左右止百餘騎從，乃整兵以俟。

translations.literal: At midday Hu'en reached Paisute east of the city; at midnight he arrived below the Kashgar Han city; left and right had only a little more than a hundred mounted followers; thereupon he arrayed troops to await.
translations.idiomatic: By midday Hu'en reached Paisute east of the city; by midnight he stood below the Chinese quarter of Kashgar with barely a hundred horsemen at his side, drew up his men, and waited.

sentences.zh: 平明，步兵至，寇騎開城出盪，虎恩率眾大戰，刺殺回酋王元林，會萬鵬亦至，復其城。

translations.literal: At daybreak infantry arrived; mounted bandits opened the city and came out to skirmish; Hu'en led the masses in great battle, stabbed and killed the Hui chieftain Wang Yuanlin; Wanpeng also arrived; the city was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the infantry came up; rebel cavalry sallied from the gates; Hu'en led a fierce fight, killed the Muslim chieftain Wang Yuanlin, and when Wanpeng arrived as well the city was recovered.

sentences.zh: 虎恩西追伯克胡里，令桂錫楨率騎旅自間道疾馳，而自率步旅繼之，前後夾擊，生擒余小虎、馬元於陣。

translations.literal: Hu'en pursued west after Bek Huli, ordered Gui Xizhen to lead the cavalry brigade by a hidden route in swift gallop, while he himself led foot troops to follow; front and rear pincered; captured alive Yu Xiaohu and Ma Yuan in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Hu'en drove west after Bek Huli, sent Gui Xizhen with the cavalry by a side road at full gallop, and followed with infantry; caught between the two columns, Yu Xiaohu and Ma Yuan were taken alive on the field.

sentences.zh: 繼复獲金相印父子，相印者，引安集延侵占南路也。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again captured Jin Xiangyin father and son; Xiangyin was the one who led Kokand to invade and occupy the southern road.
translations.idiomatic: He next captured Jin Xiangyin and his son—the men who had brought Kokand invaders to overrun the southern route.

sentences.zh: 於是新疆南路平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the southern road of Xinjiang was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With that the southern route of Xinjiang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 降敕褒嘉，改予一等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: An edict descended praising and commending; changed to grant First-class Light Chariot Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial decree praised his service and advanced him to First-class Light Chariot Commandant.

sentences.zh: 歷駐烏什、葉爾羌、和闐，赴本官。

translations.literal: He successively garrisoned at Wushi, Yarkand, and Khotan, then proceeded to his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: He was stationed in turn at Wushi, Yarkand, and Khotan before returning to his regular command.

sentences.zh: 十一年，謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he resigned on grounds of illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 越六年，出統湘軍，駐岳州，以能捕盜名，並二世職為二等男爵。

translations.literal: After six years he came out to command the Hunan army, garrisoned at Yuezhou, famed for ability to capture bandits; combined two hereditary offices as second-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he took command of Hunan troops at Yuezhou, won renown for suppressing bandits, and combined two hereditary posts into a second-class baronage.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授喀什噶爾提督，未上，留統武衛中軍十營。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed military governor of Kashgar; before assuming office he remained to command ten battalions of the Central Army of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed military governor of Kashgar but never took up the post, remaining instead to command ten battalions of the Martial Guard's central army.

sentences.zh: 拳亂起，諸將多崇奉之，獨虎恩則否。

translations.literal: The Boxer turmoil arose; many generals mostly revered and followed it; only Hu'en did not.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer movement erupted most commanders embraced it; Hu'en alone did not.

sentences.zh: 福祥攻使館，虎恩與論事榮祿前，謂遍觀諸軍，實不足敵外人。

translations.literal: Fuxiang attacked the legations; Hu'en argued the matter before Ronglu, saying having looked all around at the various armies, they truly were insufficient to oppose foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuxiang assaulted the legations, Hu'en argued before Ronglu that, having surveyed the armies, they were in truth no match for foreign troops.

sentences.zh: 福祥大怒，欲殺虎恩，榮祿以身翼蔽之，乃免。

translations.literal: Fuxiang was greatly angry and wished to kill Hu'en; Ronglu with his body winged and shielded him, and thus he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxiang was furious and meant to kill him, but Ronglu shielded Hu'en with his own body and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 令出防獲鹿，未幾，仍還湘。

translations.literal: He was ordered out to garrison Luquan; before long he still returned to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take post at Luquan, but soon returned to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，創發，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he fell ill, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he fell ill and died at home.

sentences.zh: 卹如製，附祀宗棠、松山祠。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts followed regulations; attached sacrifice at Zongtang's and Songshan's shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence honors followed statute, and he was granted secondary worship in the shrines of Zuo Zongtang and Liu Songshan.

sentences.zh: 桂錫楨，山東曲阜人。

translations.literal: Gui Xizhen was a native of Qufu in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Xizhen came from Qufu in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 從軍討捻，數遷至游擊。

translations.literal: He joined the army to suppress the Nian, and through several promotions reached battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: He took the field against the Nian rebels and rose through several promotions to battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，張總愚領餘眾與陳大喜合，勢張甚。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, Zhang Zongyu led remnant masses to join Chen Daxi; momentum spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, Zhang Zongyu united his remnant force with Chen Daxi and their power swelled.

sentences.zh: 錫楨追至河間，裹創力戰，寇大敗，錫楨名始著。

translations.literal: Xizhen pursued to Hejian, wrapped wounds and fought with force; the bandits routed greatly; Xizhen's name first became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhen pursued them to Hejian, fought on though wounded, and inflicted a crushing defeat that first made his name known.

sentences.zh: 同治七年，從左宗棠徵陝回，數獲勝，檄守同官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he followed Zuo Zongtang to campaign against Shaanxi Hui, won several times, and was ordered by dispatch to garrison Tongguan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he campaigned under Zuo Zongtang against the Shaanxi Muslims, won repeated victories, and was ordered to hold Tongguan.

sentences.zh: 明年，提督高連升屯宜君，親兵丁玉龍匪首也，構回為亂，夜圍營帳，戕統帥。

translations.literal: The next year provincial commander Gao Liansheng garrisoned Yijun; his personal soldier Ding Yulong was also a bandit chief; he incited Hui into rebellion, by night surrounded the camp tent, and killed the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Provincial Commander Gao Liansheng was posted at Yijun when his own soldier Ding Yulong, a bandit chieftain, incited the Muslims to revolt, surrounded the camp by night, and slew the commander.

sentences.zh: 錫楨聞警，亟自同官馳援，擊卻之，复追剿金鎖關、米子窯。

translations.literal: Xizhen heard the alarm, urgently from Tongguan galloped to aid, struck and repelled them, again pursued and suppressed Jinsuoguan and Miziyao.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, Xizhen galloped from Tongguan to the rescue, drove the rebels back, and pursued them through Jinsuoguan and Miziyao.

sentences.zh: 會楚軍將丁賢發等至，拘玉龍誅之，城獲全，遷參將。

translations.literal: It happened that Hunan army generals Ding Xianfa and others arrived, seized Yulong and executed him; the city was preserved whole; he was transferred to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan commanders including Ding Xianfa arrived, Yulong was seized and executed, the city was saved, and Xizhen was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 從克固原三營，斬其酋楊文治，進扼中衛四百戶。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Guyuan's three camps, beheaded their chieftain Yang Wenzhi, advanced to choke Zhongwei's four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take the three camps at Guyuan, beheaded the rebel chief Yang Wenzhi, and advanced to block Zhongwei.

sentences.zh: 回酋馬光明自固原東北入同心城，復大敗之。

translations.literal: The Hui chieftain Ma Guangming from Guyuan's northeast entered Tongxin city; he again routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslim chief Ma Guangming entered Tongxin from northeast of Guyuan, Xizhen defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 又降元城回海生春。

translations.literal: He again induced the Yuancheng Hui Hai Shengchun to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also induced the Yuancheng Muslim leader Hai Shengchun to submit.

sentences.zh: 十年，規河州，錫楨自中衛、靖遠南搜會寧遊匪。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, planning Hezhou, Xizhen from Zhongwei and Jingyuan searched south for Huining roaming bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, as operations turned toward Hezhou, Xizhen swept south from Zhongwei and Jingyuan against roving bandits around Huining.

sentences.zh: 亡何，肅州降回叛，甘、涼戒嚴，錫楨遂還軍肅州。

translations.literal: Before long Suzhou's surrendered Hui rebelled; Gansu and Liangzhou were placed on alert; Xizhen then returned his army to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the surrendered Muslims at Suzhou rebelled, Gansu and Liangzhou were placed on alert, and Xizhen marched back to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，略東關，克其大卡一，寇出拒，擊退之。

translations.literal: The next year he raided the east pass, took one of its great pass-stations; bandits came out to resist and he struck them back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked the east gate, seized one of its major outposts, and drove back the rebels who came out to resist.

sentences.zh: 先是肅回敗，倚硃家堡、黃草壩、塔爾灣、文殊山各堡，互犄角，誓死守，徐佔彪攻弗克，至是誘之出，錫楨隱卒深林，俟寇過半，橫截而出，諸軍繼之，寇大潰。

translations.literal: Earlier the Suzhou Hui defeated had relied on Zhujiabao, Huangcaoba, Ta'erwan, and Wenshushan forts, mutually corner-horned, swearing to die defending; Xu Zhanbiao's attack could not overcome them; at this time they were lured out; Xizhen hid troops in deep forest, waited until bandits were more than half past, cut across and emerged; the various armies followed; the bandits routed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the defeated Muslims at Suzhou had held Zhujiabao, Huangcaoba, Ta'erwan, and Wenshushan in mutual support and sworn to die defending them; Xu Zhanbiao had failed to take them. Now the rebels were lured out; Xizhen hid men in the forest, let more than half the column pass, then struck across their line while the other units followed, and the enemy collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 肅州西南墩堡悉平。

translations.literal: Suzhou's southwest mound-forts were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All the fortified mounds southwest of Suzhou were pacified.

sentences.zh: 進屯沙子壩，去肅城三里，肅回啟南門出盪，錫楨率騎旅突陣，回奔入城。

translations.literal: He advanced to garrison at Shaziba, three li from Suzhou city; Suzhou Hui opened the south gate and came out to skirmish; Xizhen led the cavalry brigade to rush the formation; the Hui fled back into the city.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to camp at Shaziba three li from Suzhou; the garrison sallied from the south gate, Xizhen led a cavalry charge, and the defenders fled back within the walls.

sentences.zh: 諸軍衝殺，連克四壩、十一堡，東面寇壘亦盡，賜號精勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The various armies charged and killed; in succession took four dams and eleven forts; eastern rebel fortifications also exhausted; granted the title Valiant Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: The allied columns stormed forward, took four stockades and eleven forts in succession, and cleared the enemy works on the east; he was granted the title Valiant Baturu.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從出關，錫楨率四百騎歸額爾慶額節度，進古城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed out of the pass; Xizhen led four hundred mounted troops under Erqing'e's command and advanced to Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he marched beyond the pass; Xizhen led four hundred horsemen under Erqing'e's command and advanced on Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，攻阜康。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he attacked Fukang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he attacked Fukang.

sentences.zh: 宗棠慮寇北竄，令錫楨扼沙山、馬橋備要擊。

translations.literal: Zongtang worried the bandits would flee north; ordered Xizhen to choke Shashan and Maqiao in preparation to strike vital points.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang feared the rebels might break north and ordered Xizhen to hold Shashan and Maqiao ready to intercept them.

sentences.zh: 尋會諸軍复烏魯木齊，北路略定，唯瑪納斯南城久未下。

translations.literal: Before long he joined the various armies to recover Urumqi; the northern road was roughly settled; only Manas south city long had not fallen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the other columns in recovering Urumqi and securing the northern route, though the south city of Manas still held out.

sentences.zh: 宗棠以劉錦棠軍單，檄錫楨助擊，與諸軍轟潰之，斬其酋韓金農，更勇號業普肯，擢總兵。

translations.literal: Zongtang because Liu Jintang's army was thin, dispatched Xizhen to assist the attack; with the various armies bombarded and routed them; beheaded their chieftain Han Jinnong; changed brave title to Yepuken; promoted to brigade commander.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Liu Jintang's force too thin, Zuo ordered Xizhen to reinforce the assault; together they blasted the defenders apart and slew the rebel chief Han Jinnong; Xizhen received the new brave title Yepuken and was promoted to brigade commander.

sentences.zh: 進規南路，三年，從錦棠攻克達坂，乘勝复吐魯番，晉提督。

translations.literal: He advanced to plan the southern road; in the third year he followed Jintang to overcome Daban, rode victory to recover Turfan, and was promoted to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning on the southern route, in the third year he followed Jintang in taking Daban, pressed on to recover Turfan, and was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 規喀什噶爾，錫楨統馬步二千餘人，自阿克蘇取道巴爾楚，克瑪納巴什，直抵喀城東牌素特。

translations.literal: Planning Kashgar, Xizhen commanded more than two thousand horse and foot, from Aksu took the route Barkol, took Manabashi, straight to Kashgar city's east Paisute.
translations.idiomatic: In the drive on Kashgar, Xizhen commanded more than two thousand horse and foot, marched from Aksu by way of Barkol, took Manabashi, and reached Paisute east of the city.

sentences.zh: 會黃萬鵬軍亦至麻古木，彥虎與伯克胡里潰逃，遂復西四城。

translations.literal: It happened that Huang Wanpeng's army also reached Magumu; Yanhu and Bek Huli routed in flight; thereupon the four western cities were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Wanpeng's column also reached Magumu, Bai Yanhu and Bek Huli fled in rout, and the four western cities were recovered.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: For merit he was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 回疆告寧，晉頭品秩，加賜呢鏗額勇號。

translations.literal: The Muslim frontier reported peace; promoted to first-rank grade; additionally granted the brave title Nekeng'e.
translations.idiomatic: With the Muslim frontier declared at peace, he was advanced to first-rank grade and granted the additional brave title Nekeng'e.

sentences.zh: 五年，乞歸葬親，道陝，創發，逾歲卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he requested return to bury his parents; on the road through Shaanxi he fell ill; after a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he asked leave to return and bury his parents; he fell ill on the road through Shaanxi and died a year later.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，巡撫恩壽狀其績以上，予優恤。

translations.literal: At the Xuantong reign change, Governor Enshou memorialized his achievements upward; superior condolence gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuantong reign, Governor Enshou memorialized his record to the throne and he was granted enhanced posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 方友升，湖南長沙人。

translations.literal: Fang Yousheng was a native of Changsha in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yousheng came from Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐末，從軍剿川寇，積勳至守備。

translations.literal: Late in Xianfeng he joined the army to suppress Sichuan bandits, accumulating merit until garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Xianfeng era he took the field against bandits in Sichuan and rose through merit to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 克太平，力戰，砲彈洞L6，繇是以饒勇名。

translations.literal: He captured Taiping, fought fiercely, and a cannonball pierced through him; from this he gained the name of abundant courage.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Taiping he fought fiercely; a cannonball pierced his body, and from that day he was famed for exceptional bravery.

sentences.zh: 同治七年，討陝回，克鳳翔、岐山，嘗從行，有所衝陷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he campaigned against the Shaanxi Hui, captured Fengxiang and Qishan, often followed on campaign, and made charges and breakthroughs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tongzhi he fought the Shaanxi Muslims, took Fengxiang and Qishan, and repeatedly led daring assaults on campaign.

sentences.zh: 入關隴，隸劉松山麾下。

translations.literal: Entering Guanlong, he served under Liu Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Guanlong region and served under Liu Songshan.

sentences.zh: 金積堡之役，師失利。

translations.literal: In the Jinjibao campaign the army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinjibao the army met with defeat.

sentences.zh: 會友升購馬張家口，逮歸，無收馬者，或勸之去，弗聽。

translations.literal: It happened that Yousheng was purchasing horses at Zhangjiakou; when he returned there was no one to receive the horses, and some urged him to leave, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yousheng happened to be buying horses at Zhangjiakou. When he returned, no one would take the horses, and some urged him to desert, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 驅馬數千入左宗棠軍，宗棠大器之，乃編所購馬為西征靖營隊，囑領之，遣赴河州，攻剿三甲集、太子寺。

translations.literal: He drove several thousand horses into Zuo Zongtang's army; Zongtang greatly valued him, and thus organized the purchased horses as the Western Expedition Jingying Corps, entrusted him to lead it, and sent him to Hezhou to attack and suppress Sanjiaji and Taizisi.
translations.idiomatic: He drove several thousand horses into Zuo Zongtang's camp. Zongtang thought highly of him, formed the purchased horses into the Western Expedition Jingying Corps under his command, and sent him to Hezhou to attack Sanjiaji and Taizisi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會攻肅州，其關城阻壕，壕深三四丈，古所謂酒泉也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he joined in attacking Suzhou; its pass city was blocked by a moat three or four zhang deep—the ancient so-called Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he joined the assault on Suzhou. The pass city was shielded by a moat three or four zhang deep—the ancient Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 徐佔彪乘回懈，逾壕進攻。

translations.literal: Xu Zhanbiao seized on the Hui's slackness and crossed the moat to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhanbiao took advantage of the Muslims' lapse, crossed the moat, and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 友升先登，諸軍蟻附上，奪東關，回入城死守。

translations.literal: Yousheng ascended first; the armies swarmed up like ants, seized the east gate, and the Hui withdrew into the city to defend desperately.
translations.idiomatic: Yousheng was first over the wall; the other units swarmed up after him and took the east gate. The defenders withdrew into the city and held on desperately.

sentences.zh: 佔彪築城南二卡，回來爭，友升率騎旅下馬巷戰，彈貫脛及脊骨，創甚，猶大呼殺賊，水漿不入者七日，眾感奮，克之。

translations.literal: Zhanbiao built two stockades south of the city; the Hui came to contest them; Yousheng led cavalry to dismount for lane fighting; a bullet pierced his shin and spine bone; wounded severely, he still shouted greatly to kill rebels; for seven days he took no water or broth; the masses were moved to fervor, and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanbiao built two stockades south of the city, which the Muslims tried to retake. Yousheng led his cavalry into dismounted street fighting. A bullet pierced his shin and spine. Though gravely wounded, he kept shouting to kill the enemy and took neither food nor drink for seven days. His men were inspired to redoubled effort, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 捷入，晉副將，賜號哈豐阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Victory was reported; he was advanced to deputy commander and granted the title Hafengabatulu.
translations.idiomatic: News of victory reached the court; he was promoted to deputy commander and granted the honorific Hafengabatulu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從克巴燕戎格，署鎮夷營游擊，自是別為一軍，幟色黃。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed in capturing Bayan Rongge, acted as mobile corps commander of the Zhenyi battalion, and from this formed a separate army with yellow banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he helped take Bayan Rongge and was appointed acting mobile corps commander of the Zhenyi battalion. From then on he commanded a separate force with yellow banners.

sentences.zh: 每戰從後擊殺，當者輒靡，寇見黃旗隊，輒相戒無犯雲。

translations.literal: In every battle he struck and killed from the rear; whoever faced him was routed; when rebels saw the yellow-banner corps they warned one another not to offend, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he struck from the rear and cut down the enemy; none who stood against him held firm. Rebels who saw the yellow-banner corps were said to warn one another not to provoke them.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，關隴平，擢總兵，從劉錦棠出關。

translations.literal: At the change of reign to Guangxu, Guanlong was pacified; he was promoted to regional commander and followed Liu Jintang beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Guangxu reign began and Guanlong was pacified, he was promoted to regional commander and marched beyond the pass with Liu Jintang.

sentences.zh: 三年，攻克達坂、托克遜，進复吐魯番，晉提督。

translations.literal: In the third year he captured Daban and Toksun, advanced to recover Turfan, and was promoted to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he took Daban and Toksun, went on to recover Turfan, and was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 以次下阿克蘇、烏什、庫車及天山南北二路。

translations.literal: In succession he took Aksu, Ush, Kuche, and the two routes north and south of the Tianshan.
translations.idiomatic: In turn he captured Aksu, Ush, Kuche, and the cities along both routes north and south of the Tianshan.

sentences.zh: 論功，賞黃馬褂，賜頭品秩。

translations.literal: In reckoning merit he was rewarded with the yellow jacket and granted first-rank rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he received the yellow jacket and first-rank court rank.

sentences.zh: 五年，安集延、布魯特寇邊，徑抵烏魯克恰提。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Kokand and Kirghiz raided the border, reaching straight to Wulukeqia.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Kokand and Kirghiz forces raided the frontier and pushed as far as Wulukeqia.

sentences.zh: 友升先進烏帕爾覘虛實。

translations.literal: Yousheng advanced first to Wupa'er to reconnoiter strength and weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Yousheng went ahead to Wupa'er to scout the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 越數日，報寇騎已入烏帕拉特。

translations.literal: After several days it was reported that rebel cavalry had already entered Wupala.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later word came that enemy horsemen had entered Wupala.

sentences.zh: 獲寇諜，訊知其乘夜襲營，諸軍備往擊，大破之。

translations.literal: They captured a rebel spy, interrogated and learned they would raid the camp by night; all armies prepared to go strike and routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: They captured an enemy spy and learned of a planned night assault. The troops lay in wait and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 友升與楊金龍分左右入，軍士皆奮迅超躍，寇不能成陣，還遁俄羅斯。

translations.literal: Yousheng and Yang Jinlong entered from left and right; soldiers all strove and leaped forward; the rebels could not form battle lines and fled back into Russia.
translations.idiomatic: Yousheng and Yang Jinlong attacked from left and right. The soldiers charged with furious energy; the enemy could not hold formation and fled back into Russian territory.

sentences.zh: 八年，入關，遭母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he entered the pass and, suffering his mother's mourning, returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he returned inside the pass and went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越事起，出頓憑祥，進攻文淵，陷重圍，彈傷手斷筋，親軍五百止存二十七騎，卒潰圍出。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; he went out to station at Pingxiang, advanced to attack Wenyuan, fell into heavy encirclement, was wounded by bullet in hand with severed sinew; of five hundred personal troops only twenty-seven riders remained; in the end he broke the encirclement and emerged.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when war broke out with France over Vietnam, he stationed at Pingxiang and advanced on Wenyuan. Caught in a tight encirclement, he was shot in the hand and his tendons were severed. Of his five hundred personal guards only twenty-seven horsemen survived, yet he finally broke out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷宥其敗，且嘉勞之。

translations.literal: The court pardoned his defeat and moreover praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The court forgave his defeat and commended him for his efforts.

sentences.zh: 复諒山、長慶，予世職，除廣東南韶連鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He again recovered Langshan and Changqing, was granted a hereditary office, and was appointed regional commander of the Nanshao-Lian garrison in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Langshan and Changqing, received a hereditary rank, and was appointed regional commander of the Nanshao-Lian garrison in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入覲，上視傷痕，為惻然。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered court audience; the emperor viewed his wound scars and was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he came to court; the emperor examined his scars and was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 尋解任。

translations.literal: Soon he was relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed from his post.

sentences.zh: 中日失和，領三千人北上，守山海關。

translations.literal: When China and Japan fell out, he led three thousand men north to guard Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan broke out, he led three thousand men north to defend Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 拳亂作，复率師入衛，駐山西固關。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, he again led troops to enter the capital guard and garrisoned Guguan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, he again brought his troops to the capital for guard duty and was stationed at Guguan in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，調浙江衢州鎮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to the Quzhou garrison in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to command the Quzhou garrison in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 設講武堂，以新法訓練其眾，並修復柘水故道，民德之。

translations.literal: He established a military academy, trained his masses by new methods, and also restored the old course of the Zhe River; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a military academy and drilled his troops in modern methods, and also restored the old channel of the Zhe River; the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，創發，卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he fell ill; he died, and condolence followed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he fell ill and died; standard mourning honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 論曰：初討陝回，福祥以降軍效力，名震西域，何其悍也！

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the first campaign against the Shaanxi Hui, Fuxiang as a surrendered army rendered service; his name shook the Western Regions—how fierce he was!
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In the early campaigns against the Shaanxi Muslims, Dong Fuxiang fought as a surrendered rebel turned loyalist and made his name feared throughout the Western Regions—what ferocity!

sentences.zh: 運昌統卓勝軍，萬鵬領旌善營，與虎恩、錫楨、友升轉戰寧、肅，皆以驍勇名，各著奇績，其勇略亦有可傳焉。

translations.literal: Yunchang commanded the Zhuosheng Army, Wanpeng led the Jingshan battalion, and with Hu'en, Xizhen, and Yousheng they campaigned in turn through Ning and Su— all were famed for fierce courage, each achieved extraordinary merit, and their bravery and strategy are also worth transmitting.
translations.idiomatic: Yunchang commanded the Zhuosheng Army and Wanpeng the Jingshan battalion; together with Yu Huen, Gui Xizhen, and Fang Yousheng they fought across Ningxia and Gansu, all famed for valor and each recording remarkable feats—their courage and strategy are likewise worth recounting.

sentences.zh: 其後福祥終以驕妄敗，助亂啟釁，竟免顯戮，豈非幸歟？

translations.literal: Afterward Fuxiang in the end was ruined by arrogance and presumption, aided turmoil and provoked conflict, yet escaped conspicuous execution—is this not fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end Fuxiang was undone by arrogance, fomented disorder, and provoked foreign war—only to escape the death penalty. Was he not fortunate indeed?
